Thank you for taking part. COSMIC is bringing together cognitive test data from ageing studies around the world, using the Harmonized Cognitive Assessment Protocol (HCAP) as the reference. Before any statistics, we need expert judgement on two things: what each test measures, and which tests are similar enough across studies to act as links between them.

You will see 18 tests, one per page. Each page starts with a reference panel describing the test as it was given in one study. Please judge that version, not the test in general. Existing classifications are deliberately not shown.

For each test we ask: which cognitive domain it mainly measures; any other domains; how confident you are; what else might affect scores; and, where there is a comparison item, whether the two could be linked.

Your answers are confidential. They are stored under a code, not your name, and only the moderator can match codes to people. Please answer on your own and do not discuss your answers with other panel members. In Round 2 you will see the group's anonymised answers next to your own.

The six domains used in this questionnaire
Orientation: knowing the current time, date and place.
Memory: learning new information and recalling or recognising it later.
Attention / processing speed: focusing and sustaining attention, and the speed of simple mental operations.
Executive function: controlling and organising thinking: switching, inhibition, holding and manipulating information, reasoning, planning.
Language: understanding and producing words and sentences: naming, comprehension, repetition, word retrieval, reading, writing.
Visuospatial / constructional: perceiving spatial relations and copying or constructing figures.
These definitions are repeated under the first question on every page.
